# Synthetic data design

**Every row in this repository's datasets is synthetic.** The data was generated by
[`src/nps_analysis/generate_data.py`](../src/nps_analysis/generate_data.py) with a fixed random seed (`2024`), so anyone can regenerate the
same file. It does not contain, and is not derived from, real survey responses, client data or brand performance figures.

## Why synthetic data

The original customer-experience research I worked on is confidential, and I no longer have access to it. Rather than present
invented results as real, this project builds a realistic *stand-in* dataset with **known, documented assumptions**, then shows
that the cleaning and analysis code recovers those assumptions (see the "Method check" section of the report).

## How a response is generated

For each respondent the generator draws a market, then a brand (using a per-market brand mix), a usage type (personal vs
commercial) and an ownership duration (gamma-distributed, mostly under three years). It then computes a latent
"advocacy" value on the 0-10 scale:

```
advocacy = 7.2 + market effect + brand effect + brand×market interaction
               + ownership-duration effect + usage effect + Normal(0, 1.9)
```

The NPS answer is that value rounded and clipped to 0-10. Satisfaction (CSAT, 1-5) is derived from the same value plus extra noise,
so the two are correlated but not identical.

| Assumption | Value (points on the 0-10 scale) |
|---|---|
| Market effect | Philippines +0.35, Nigeria +0.15, Egypt -0.10, DR Congo -0.55 |
| Brand effect | TVS +0.10, Bajaj +0.05, Haojue -0.25 |
| Brand × market interaction | Haojue in the Philippines +0.45, TVS in DR Congo -0.30 |
| Ownership duration | 0-6 m +0.45, 6-12 m +0.15, 12-24 m -0.45, 24-36 m -0.20, 36+ m +0.05 |
| Usage | Personal +0.10, Commercial -0.25 |
| Commercial share | Nigeria 55%, Egypt 30%, Philippines 45%, DR Congo 60% |

These values are illustrative choices, not estimates of any real market. The brand effects were deliberately kept small, so the
analysis also shows what happens when a sample is too small to detect a difference.

## Comments and feedback categories

- Detractors (and about half of the passives) get a comment about a "pain" topic, drawn from a market-specific distribution
  (e.g. spare-parts availability is weighted more heavily in DR Congo, price in Egypt, dealer experience in the Philippines).
  Promoters get a comment about a "praise" topic.
- Comments come from short templates. To make text analysis non-trivial: 8% are vague ("Not happy."), 15% mention a second topic,
  and 8% of responses have a recorded `feedback_category` that does not match the comment, as happens when a respondent or
  interviewer ticks the wrong box.

## Data-quality problems injected on purpose

| Problem | Approx. share |
|---|---|
| Country spelling variants (`NG`, `DRC`, `The Philippines`, trailing spaces) | 6% |
| Brand spelling variants (`TVS Motor`, `bajaj`, `HAOJUE`) | 5% |
| NPS missing / non-numeric (`ten`, `9/10`) / outside 0-10 | 2.6% |
| CSAT outside 1-5 or missing | 2.5% |
| Ownership duration negative, > 120 months or text | 1.4% |
| Dates in dd/mm/yyyy or outside 2024 | 2.4% |
| Blank or placeholder comments | 3% |
| Missing customer ID | 0.2% |
| Exact duplicate submissions | 1.2% |

The cleaning step ([`clean.py`](../src/nps_analysis/clean.py)) handles each of these with an explicit, logged rule.
